FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Anyone driving a motor vehicle, motor-driven cycle or moped on public roads in Colorado has to be at least 16 years old and carry a valid driver license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Once you become a Colorado resident, you have 30 days to get a Colorado driver license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Colorado counts you as a resident if, for example, you own or run a business in the state, have lived there continuously for 90 days, or hold a job there. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
The 30-day licensing deadline does not apply to active-duty U.S. military members, their dependents, or people living in Colorado mainly to further their education. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
If your name or address changes, you must tell the Division of Motor Vehicles within 30 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
The written knowledge test draws on the whole handbook, including road signs, driving under the influence, driving rules, safety rules and legal topics; practice quizzes are offered online and in the myColorado app. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
Offices stop giving written tests 30 minutes before their scheduled closing time, so arrive earlier than that. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
Passing a written test makes you eligible for an instruction permit, which gives a learner limited driving privileges. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
While driving on an instruction permit, you need a supervising driver aged 21 or older, holding a valid Colorado license, in the front passenger seat. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
State driver license offices do not currently schedule drive tests; some county-run offices do, and most drive tests are given by certified commercial driving schools. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
Before a drive test the examiner checks the vehicle for safety, including brake lights, turn signals, seat belts, windshield and tires, and confirms the doors and windows open from inside; a vehicle you supply needs current insurance and registration. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A01
During the drive test only you and the examiner may be in the car: no interpreters, family, friends or pets; remove any weapons, switch off the radio, phone and other electronics, and clear the dashboard and rearview mirror. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A01
If you fail the drive test, you cannot retake it until the next business day. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A01
The examiner will never ask you to break the law; ask your questions before the test starts, because you are scored the entire time and extra talking only interferes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A01
The drive test follows AAMVA guidelines and assesses three skill categories: perceptual (seeing gaps and hazards), motor (operating the controls) and attentional (focusing and shifting attention). [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A01
Your drive test score comes from six maneuvers: left and right turns, stopping at intersections, driving through intersections, changing lanes in traffic, general driving behavior, and merging into and leaving traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A01
Lane selection is graded: enter and leave traffic from the correct lane, approach intersections in the correct lane, and finish each maneuver in the correct lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A01
Lane management is graded: stay entirely within the turning lane, keep both hands on the wheel, and steer with an approved method such as hand-over-hand or push-pull-slide. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
When turning right, start from the right-most part of your lane; when turning left, start from the left-most part of your lane [A02] [A01].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
After a turn, settle the car in the center of the proper lane and never cross lane markings or ride over curbs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
Keep your turn signal on continuously for 100 feet before turning or changing lanes in urban areas, and for 200 feet before doing so on four-lane highways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
Cancel your turn signal within 3 seconds after you finish the turn or lane change. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
Good speed control means slowing smoothly without holding up traffic, keeping a steady speed through a lane change, and reaching an intersection slowly enough to turn without braking mid-turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A02
A correct stop has no forward motion, stays behind the stop line and crosswalk, and keeps the front wheels pointed straight until you begin the turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A02
When stopped behind another vehicle, you are far enough back if you can see where its rear tires touch the pavement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A02
Accelerate smoothly: do not jerk, lug the engine, coast, clash gears, stall, or hold up traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A02
Searching means scanning traffic, checking over your shoulder before a lane change, using mirrors, looking left, right, then left again before entering an intersection, and looking behind after every turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A02
Back-up cameras and blind-spot or lane-departure warnings may be used during the drive test, but they never replace your own physical searching. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A02
Applicants under 18 must include an Affidavit of Liability (form DR2460), signed by a parent, stepparent, grandparent with power of attorney, legal guardian, spouse over 18, or another responsible adult who accepts legal liability. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A02
The affidavit is signed before a driver license office employee or a notary; the signer becomes legally responsible for your driving and may withdraw, which cancels your permit or license; minors in foster care can be exempt under certain conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A02
A minor must hold an instruction permit for 12 months before applying for a driver license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A02
A minor applicant must turn in a signed driving log showing 50 hours of driving, including 10 hours at night. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A02
Applicants younger than 16 and 6 months must also complete 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training with an approved driver education instructor. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A02
If no approved school within 30 miles of home offers at least 20 hours of behind-the-wheel training per week, 12 extra hours with a parent, guardian or alternate permit supervisor may replace the 6 instructor hours; bring a printed route map if the nearest commercial school is more than 30 miles away. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A02
For the first six months after a driver under 18 is licensed, no passengers under 21 are allowed unless a parent or another licensed adult driver is in the car. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A02
From 6 months to 1 year of licensure, a driver under 18 may carry one passenger under 21, with siblings and passengers in a medical emergency as exceptions; after 1 year, passengers may equal the number of seat belts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A02
During the first year of licensure, a minor may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. unless accompanied by an instructor, parent or legal guardian; exceptions cover trips to school or work with a signed statement, medical emergencies and emancipated minors. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A02
Your driving privilege can be suspended, revoked or canceled if you reach the point total for suspension, are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or refuse an alcohol or drug test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A02
Leaving a crash scene without stopping, exchanging information and giving aid, or failing to report a crash to the DMV under the Financial Responsibility Law, can also cost you your license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A02
Other grounds for losing your license include lying on your application, not settling a crash judgment, lending or misusing your license, skipping a DMV re-examination, and a vehicular homicide conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0005]
